newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE TO LAUNCH NEW 2-YR ZERO COUPON T-NOTE JAN 20.
newsitem.headline: GREECE TO LAUNCH NEW 2-YR ZERO COUPON T-NOTE JAN 20.

text.p: Greece will issue a new two-year zero coupon T-note January 20 along with other issues of 12-month T-bills and an auction of seven-year FRNs and three-year fixed coupon bonds in January, the finance ministry said.
The new state debt paper aims to cover a borrowing need of 1.5 trillion drachmas in January, deputy finance minister Nickos Christodoulakis told a press conference.
He said the country's public debt improved a touch in 1996 to 35.6 trillion drachmas or 120.5 percent of GDP.
This was part of the reason for a recent credit rating upgrade by Moody's which improved Greece's ranking to 34th from 40th, he said.
Beginning on January 2, the finance ministry will issue 12-month T-bills at 11.20 percent, six-month T-bills at 10.50 percent and three-month T-bills at 10.20 percent.

"The rate on the new T-bills was kept at 11.20 percent in order to ease the light impact on yield as a result of the new 7.5 percent tax on earned interest that goes into effect in 1997," Christodoulakis said.
State debt paper enjoyed a tax exempt status but this ends Dec 31 1996.
He specified that the new 7.5 percent tax will be witheld on purchases of all new T-bill issues.
But on all other debt issues like floaters, two-year T-notes and three-year coupon bonds the tax will be paid upon maturity, the deputy finance minister said.
The Bank of Greece is expected to announce soon its decision on procedures for tax reimbursement by foreign buyers of Greek debt securities to avoid double taxation, he said.

Greece will issue a new two-year zero coupon T-note on January 20. And an auction of seven-year floaters and three-year fixed-coupon bonds is planned for January 24. The issue date will be January 27.

Finally, another issue of 12-month T-bills and two-year T-notes is scheduled for January 31, Christodoulakis said. He did not specify rates but said these would depend on prevailing market conditions at the time. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
